# PLAN — iteration 1

## Current state assessment

The `mux4` seed is a single-cycle registered 4:1, 8-bit mux with synchronous active-high reset to zero and no enable or parameters. The verified incumbent uses 8 LUTs and 8 FFs and is timing-feasible at WNS 0.579 ns and WHS 0.052 ns; there is no register-to-register timing path. The objective is fewer LUTs, while preserving the exact ports and cycle behavior. Top numeric latency is unknown, so no numeric `@latency` annotation is required.

## Hypothesis

Replacing the `case` mux with explicit one-hot select decode and per-input masked OR logic may map to fewer LUTs on the 7-series fabric while retaining the existing output register; this must be confirmed by routed utilization and timing reports.

## Instruction for generator

Keep the existing `always @(posedge clk)` reset and output-register behavior, but replace the `case (sel)` data selection with four mutually exclusive `sel` equality terms that mask `a`, `b`, `c`, and `d`, then OR the masked 8-bit values into `y`. Preserve synchronous active-high reset to `8'd0`, the same input-to-output cycle, and all 8 data bits for every selector value. Do not add registers or a numeric latency annotation; promote only if the unchanged verification gates pass, routed setup WNS and hold WHS are nonnegative, and LUT count strictly improves against the incumbent.
